We recently had Cryptowall attack our work network (encrypting files) due to an unprotected PC downloading it - it then spread through our network drives doing stupid amounts of damage. Luckily we have daily backups that go off-site otherwise I imagine it could easily take down a company.

Calling these people "hackers" is a little hyperbolic. Generally someone develops a kit that allows people that are technical, but not enough to develop an exploit, to use someone else's exploit to ransom people. There was a news article recently about a site operating on Tor that does this, I can't recall the name. Essentially, you sign up and then it gives you an option of a few different pieces of malware that will encrypt the victim's system. The virus reports back whether it has infected the computer, allowing you to track how successful it is, and it will retrieve the amount you want in ransom (which is pretty much just a sliding bar). If you get paid, the person who owns the site gets something like 10% of the ransom and you get the rest.

It's a big development because you no longer need to know about the bowels of a computer to be able to spread ransomware, which is part of the reason for the huge upturn in it.
I suppose I'm not surprised to see ransomware and exploit kits topping the list.
